summary: The Torah forbids shechting a mother animal and its child on the same day ("oso v'es b'no"). This rule applies everywhere and always, for plain animals and for korbanos, and the mishnah shows what happens in different cases.

chunks.en: The rule of "it and its child"
chunks.explain: Not to shecht a mother animal and its child on the same day.
chunks.st: The prohibition against slaughtering an animal itself and its offspring

chunks.he: נוֹהֵג בֵּין בָּאָרֶץ בֵּין בְּחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ,
chunks.en: applies both in Eretz Yisrael and outside Eretz Yisrael,
chunks.st: applies both in Eretz Yisrael and outside of Eretz Yisrael, both

chunks.en: both when the Beis HaMikdash stands and when it does not,
chunks.st: in the presence, i.e., the time, of the Temple and not in the presence of the Temple, and it applies

chunks.en: with plain animals and with korbanos.
chunks.st: with regard to non-sacred animals and with regard to sacrificial animals.

chunks.he: כֵּיצַד. הַשּׁוֹחֵט אוֹתוֹ וְאֶת בְּנוֹ חֻלִּין בַּחוּץ,
chunks.en: How so? Someone who shechts it and its child, both plain animals, outside:
chunks.st: How so? In the case of one who slaughters an animal itself and its offspring,

chunks.en: both of them are kosher,
chunks.st: both of which are non-sacred, and slaughters them outside the Temple courtyard, both of the animals are fit for consumption,

chunks.en: and for the second one he gets the forty lashes.
chunks.explain: Malkus, the punishment for breaking certain Torah laws.
chunks.st: but for slaughtering the second animal, one incurs [sofeg] the forty lashes
chunks.stMore: for violating the prohibition: “You shall not slaughter it and its offspring both in one day” (Leviticus 22:28).

chunks.en: If they were korbanos, shechted outside the Beis HaMikdash:
chunks.st: If both animals were sacrificial animals slaughtered outside the Temple courtyard,

chunks.en: for the first one he deserves kares,
chunks.explain: Kares is a punishment from Heaven.
chunks.st: then for slaughtering the first animal, one is liable to receive excision from the World-to-Come [karet].
chunks.stMore: For slaughtering the second animal one is not liable to receive karet. The second animal was not fit for sacrifice, since one may not slaughter an animal and its offspring on the same day.

chunks.en: and both of them are pasul,
chunks.st: And both animals are disqualified for use as offerings,

chunks.en: and for both of them he gets the forty lashes.
chunks.st: and for the slaughter of both of them, one incurs forty lashes apiece:
chunks.stMore: The first being a sacrificial animal slaughtered outside the courtyard and the second being the offspring of an animal slaughtered that day.

chunks.en: Plain animals shechted inside:
chunks.st: If both animals were non-sacred and slaughtered inside the Temple courtyard,

chunks.en: both of them are pasul,
chunks.st: both of them are unfit to be sacrificed, being non-sacred animals slaughtered in the courtyard.

chunks.en: and for the second one he gets the forty lashes.
chunks.st: And for slaughter of the second animal, one incurs the forty lashes for slaughtering an animal and its offspring on a single day.

chunks.en: Korbanos shechted inside:
chunks.st: If both animals were sacrificial animals slaughtered inside the Temple courtyard,

chunks.en: the first one is kosher, and he is free of punishment,
chunks.st: the first is fit for sacrifice, and one who slaughters it is exempt from any punishment.

chunks.en: and for the second one he gets the forty lashes, and it is pasul.
chunks.st: But for slaughter of the second animal, one incurs the forty lashes for slaughtering an animal and its offspring on a single day, and it is unfit for sacrifice, because one was not allowed to slaughter it on that day.

summary: More cases of shechting a mother and its child on one day, when one is a plain animal and one a korban, or when one is shechted inside the Beis HaMikdash and one outside.

chunks.en: A plain animal, then a korban, outside:
chunks.st: If the first animal was non-sacred and the second a sacrificial animal, and both were slaughtered outside the Temple courtyard,

chunks.en: the first is kosher, and he is free of punishment,
chunks.st: the first is fit for consumption and one who slaughters it is exempt from any punishment.

chunks.en: and for the second he gets the forty lashes, and it is pasul.
chunks.st: But for slaughtering the second animal, one incurs the forty lashes for slaughtering an animal and its offspring on a single day, and the animal is unfit for sacrifice.

chunks.en: A korban, then a plain animal, outside:
chunks.st: If the first animal was a sacrificial animal and the second was non-sacred and both were slaughtered outside the Temple courtyard,

chunks.en: for the first he deserves kares, and it is pasul,
chunks.st: for the first animal, one is liable to receive karet for slaughtering a sacrificial animal outside the courtyard, and the animal is unfit for sacrifice.

chunks.en: and the second is kosher,
chunks.st: And the second is fit for consumption;

chunks.en: and for both of them he gets the forty lashes.
chunks.st: and for the slaughter of both of them one incurs forty lashes apiece:
chunks.stMore: The first being a sacrificial animal slaughtered outside the courtyard and the second being the offspring of an animal slaughtered that day.

chunks.en: A plain animal, then a korban, inside:
chunks.st: If the first animal was non-sacred and the second was a sacrificial animal and both were slaughtered inside the Temple courtyard,

chunks.en: both of them are pasul,
chunks.st: both of them are unfit for sacrifice.

chunks.en: and for the second he gets the forty lashes.
chunks.st: And for slaughtering the second animal, one incurs the forty lashes.

chunks.en: A korban, then a plain animal, inside:
chunks.st: If the first animal was a sacrificial animal and the second was non-sacred and both were slaughtered inside the Temple courtyard,

chunks.en: the first is kosher, and he is free of punishment,
chunks.st: the first is fit for sacrifice and one who slaughters it is exempt from any punishment.

chunks.en: and for the second he gets the forty lashes, and it is pasul.
chunks.st: And for slaughtering the second animal, one incurs the forty lashes, and the animal is unfit for sacrifice, as it is non-sacred.

chunks.en: Plain animals, outside and then inside:
chunks.st: If both animals were non-sacred, and one slaughters them, the first outside the Temple courtyard and the second inside the Temple courtyard,

chunks.en: the first is kosher, and he is free of punishment,
chunks.st: the first is fit for consumption and one who slaughters it is exempt from any punishment.

chunks.en: and for the second he gets the forty lashes, and it is pasul.
chunks.st: And for slaughtering the second animal, one incurs the forty lashes for slaughtering an animal and its offspring on a single day, and the animal is unfit for sacrifice as it is non-sacred.

chunks.en: Korbanos, outside and then inside:
chunks.st: If both animals were sacrificial animals, and one slaughters them, the first outside the Temple courtyard and the second inside the Temple courtyard,

chunks.en: for the first he deserves kares,
chunks.st: for slaughtering the first animal one is liable to receive karet,

chunks.he: וּשְׁנֵיהֶם פְּסוּלִים, וּשְׁנֵיהֶם סוֹפְגִים אֶת הָאַרְבָּעִים.
chunks.en: and both of them are pasul, and for both of them he gets the forty lashes.
chunks.st: and for slaughtering both of them one incurs forty lashes apiece. One set of lashes is given because the first was a sacrificial animal slaughtered outside the courtyard, and the second set of lashes is given because the second animal is the offspring of an animal slaughtered that day. And both of them are unfit for sacrifice.

chunks.en: Plain animals, inside and then outside:
chunks.st: If both animals were non-sacred, and one slaughters them, the first inside the Temple courtyard and the second outside the Temple courtyard,

chunks.en: the first is pasul, and he is free of punishment,
chunks.st: the first is unfit for sacrifice, as it is non-sacred, and the one who slaughters it is exempt.

chunks.en: and for the second he gets the forty lashes, and it is kosher.
chunks.st: And for the second, one incurs the forty lashes and the animal is fit for consumption.

chunks.en: Korbanos, inside and then outside:
chunks.st: If both animals were sacrificial animals, and one slaughters them, the first inside the Temple courtyard and the second outside the Temple courtyard,

chunks.en: the first is kosher, and he is free of punishment,
chunks.st: the first is fit for sacrifice and one who slaughters it is exempt.

chunks.en: and for the second he gets the forty lashes, and it is pasul.
chunks.st: And for the second animal, one incurs the forty lashes, and the animal is unfit for sacrifice because its requisite time has not yet arrived.

summary: More laws of "it and its child": which shechitos count, who shechts first when two people buy a mother and child, and when a seller must tell the buyer that he sold the mother or child that day.

chunks.en: Someone who shechts and it turns out to be a treifah,
chunks.st: With regard to one who slaughters an animal and its offspring and one of them is discovered to be an animal with a wound that would have caused it to die within twelve months [tereifa] and may not be eaten,

chunks.en: someone who shechts for avodah zarah,
chunks.st: or one who slaughters one of the animals for the sake of idol worship,
chunks.stMore: from which deriving benefit is prohibited,

chunks.en: or who shechts the parah adumah,
chunks.st: or one who slaughters the red heifer of purification,

chunks.en: or an ox that was going to be stoned,
chunks.explain: An ox that killed a person.
chunks.st: or an ox that was to have been stoned,

chunks.en: or an eglah arufah,
chunks.st: or a heifer whose neck was to have been broken, all of which are animals from which deriving benefit is prohibited,

words.note: The calf whose neck is broken when a dead person is found.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says he is not punished,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon deems one who slaughters them exempt from lashes for the slaughter of a mother and its offspring,
chunks.stMore: as in his opinion, slaughter that does not render the animal fit for consumption is not considered slaughter and does not violate the prohibition.

chunks.en: and the Sages say he is punished.
chunks.st: And the Rabbis deem him liable,
chunks.stMore: as the slaughter need not render the animal fit for consumption in order to violate the prohibition.

chunks.en: Someone who shechts and it becomes a neveilah in his hand,
chunks.st: All agree that one who slaughters an animal and it becomes a carcass by his hand because the slaughter was invalid,

chunks.en: or who stabs it, or who rips out the simanim,
chunks.st: or one who stabs an animal, or one who uproots the windpipe and the gullet, is

chunks.en: is free from "it and its child."
chunks.st: exempt with regard to the prohibition against slaughtering a mother and its offspring,
chunks.stMore: as it is written: “You shall not slaughter it and its offspring both in one day” (Leviticus 22:28), and in these cases, no ritual slaughter was performed.

chunks.en: Two people who bought a cow and its child:
chunks.st: With regard to two people who purchased a cow and its offspring, where each purchased one of the animals,

chunks.en: whoever bought first
chunks.st: whoever purchased his animal first

chunks.en: shall shecht first.
chunks.st: shall slaughter it first,
chunks.stMore: and the second one must wait until the next day to slaughter his animal, so as not to violate the prohibition of: It and its offspring.

chunks.en: But if the second one went first,
chunks.st: But if the second one preceded him and slaughtered his animal first, he

chunks.he: זָכָה. שָׁחַט פָּרָה וְאַחַר כָּךְ שְׁנֵי בָנֶיהָ,
chunks.en: he gained. If he shechted a cow and then two of its children,
chunks.st: benefitted, and the one who purchased the animal first may not slaughter it until the next day. If one slaughtered a cow and thereafter slaughtered its two offspring on the same day,

chunks.en: he gets eighty lashes.
chunks.st: he incurs eighty lashes
chunks.stMore: for two separate actions violating the prohibition against slaughtering the mother and the offspring on the same day.

chunks.he: שָׁחַט שְׁנֵי בָנֶיהָ וְאַחַר כָּךְ שְׁחָטָהּ,
chunks.en: If he shechted its two children and then shechted it,
chunks.st: If one slaughtered its two offspring and thereafter slaughtered the mother cow,

chunks.en: he gets the forty lashes.
chunks.st: he incurs the forty lashes,
chunks.stMore: as he performed a single prohibited act.

chunks.he: שְׁחָטָהּ וְאֶת בִּתָּהּ וְאֶת בַּת בִּתָּהּ,
chunks.en: If he shechted it, and its daughter, and its granddaughter,
chunks.st: If one slaughtered the mother and its daughter, and, later that day, slaughtered its daughter’s daughter,

chunks.en: he gets eighty lashes.
chunks.st: he incurs eighty lashes,
chunks.stMore: as he has performed the act of slaughtering a mother and its offspring twice.

chunks.en: If he shechted it, and its granddaughter, and then
chunks.st: But if one slaughtered the mother and its daughter’s daughter

chunks.en: he shechted its daughter,
chunks.st: and thereafter slaughtered its daughter,

chunks.en: he gets the forty lashes.
chunks.st: he incurs the forty lashes,
chunks.stMore: as he performed a single prohibited act.

chunks.en: Sumchos says in the name of Rabbi Meir:
chunks.st: Sumakhos says in the name of Rabbi Meir:

chunks.en: He gets eighty lashes.
chunks.st: He incurs eighty lashes
chunks.stMore: for slaughtering the daughter on the same day as its calf and its mother, as that act comprises two separate violations of the prohibition.

chunks.en: At four times in the year, one who sells
chunks.st: On four occasions during the year one who sells

chunks.en: an animal to his friend must tell him:
chunks.st: an animal to another is required to inform him:

chunks.en: "I sold its mother to be shechted,"
chunks.st: I sold the mother of this animal today for the buyer to slaughter it,or:

chunks.en: or "I sold its daughter to be shechted."
chunks.st: I sold the daughter of this animal today for the buyer to slaughter it.

chunks.en: And these are the times:
chunks.st: And those four occasions are:

chunks.he: עֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב הָאַחֲרוֹן שֶׁל חָג,
chunks.en: Erev the last Yom Tov of Sukkos,
chunks.st: The eve of the last day of the festival of Sukkot,

chunks.he: וְעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל פֶּסַח,
chunks.en: and Erev the first Yom Tov of Pesach,
chunks.st: the eve of the first day of the festival of Passover,

chunks.en: and Erev Shavuos,
chunks.st: and the eve of Shavuot,

chunks.en: and Erev Rosh Hashanah.
chunks.st: and the eve of Rosh HaShana.

chunks.en: And according to Rabbi Yosei HaGelili,
chunks.st: And according to the statement of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili,

words.en: and according to the words of

chunks.en: also Erev Yom Kippur in the Galil.
chunks.explain: People eat a big meal before the fast.
chunks.st: the eve of Yom Kippur in the Galilee is included as well.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah said:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda said:

chunks.en: When? When there is no time in between the sales.
chunks.st: When must he inform the buyer on those days? He must do so at a time when the seller has no interval between the sale of the mother and the offspring, as they were both sold on that day.

chunks.en: But if there is time in between,
chunks.st: But if the seller has an interval between the sales,

chunks.en: he does not need to tell him.
chunks.st: he does not need to inform the buyer,
chunks.stMore: as presumably each buyer purchased the animal to slaughter it on the day he purchased it.

chunks.en: And Rabbi Yehudah agrees that one who sells
chunks.st: And Rabbi Yehuda concedes that in a case

chunks.en: the mother to the chassan and the daughter to the kallah
chunks.st: where one sells the mother animal to the groom and the offspring to the bride, that even if he did not sell them on the same day,

chunks.en: must tell,
chunks.st: he must inform the buyer, as it is

chunks.en: since we know both will shecht on the same day.
chunks.st: obvious that they are both planning to slaughter their animal on one day,
chunks.stMore: for their wedding feast.

summary: On these four busy days before Yom Tov, a butcher can be forced to shecht for even one customer. That is why on those days, if the ox dies, the buyer loses his money; on other days the seller loses.

chunks.en: At these four times, we make
chunks.st: On those four occasions,

chunks.en: the butcher shecht even if he does not want to.
chunks.st: one compels the butcher to slaughter animals even against his will;

chunks.en: Even an ox worth a thousand dinars,
chunks.st: even if there is a bull worth one thousand dinars

chunks.en: and the buyer has only one dinar,
chunks.st: and the buyer has only one dinar worth of meat,
chunks.stMore: i.e., he already paid the butcher for one dinar’s worth of meat,

chunks.en: we force him to shecht.
chunks.st: one compels him to slaughter the animal and give him a dinar’s worth of meat.

chunks.en: So if it dies,
chunks.st: Therefore, if the bull dies before slaughter, although no act of acquisition was performed,

chunks.en: it dies at the buyer's loss.
chunks.st: it dies at the expense of the buyer,
chunks.stMore: and he loses his dinar.

chunks.en: But during the rest of the year,
chunks.st: But during the rest of the days of the year

chunks.en: it is not so.
chunks.st: it is not so.
chunks.stMore: On other days, until the buyer performs the act of pulling to assume ownership of the portion of the bull that he is purchasing, the bull remains in the butcher’s possession.

chunks.en: So if it dies,
chunks.st: Therefore, if the bull dies before the transaction is complete,

chunks.en: it dies at the seller's loss.
chunks.st: it dies at the expense of the seller,
chunks.stMore: who returns the buyer’s money.

summary: The "one day" of "it and its child" starts at night and goes until the end of the next day. Ben Zoma learned this from the days of Creation, where night comes first.

chunks.he: יוֹם אֶחָד הָאָמוּר בְּאוֹתוֹ וְאֶת בְּנוֹ,
chunks.en: The "one day" said about "it and its child":
chunks.st: With regard to the phrase “one day” that is stated with regard to the prohibition against slaughtering an animal itself and its offspring,

chunks.en: the day goes after the night.
chunks.explain: Each day begins with the night before it.
chunks.st: the day follows the night.
chunks.stMore: Therefore, one may slaughter an animal during the day and slaughter its offspring that night, but one may not slaughter an animal at night and slaughter its offspring the following day.

chunks.he: אֶת זוֹ דָרַשׁ שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן זוֹמָא.
chunks.en: Shimon ben Zoma explained this.
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon ben Zoma derived this by means of a verbal analogy.

chunks.en: It says in the story of Creation (Bereishis 1):
chunks.st: It is stated in the act of Creation: “

chunks.en: "one day,"
chunks.st: One day” (Genesis 1:5),

chunks.en: and it says about "it and its child" (Vayikra 22):
chunks.st: and it is stated with regard to the slaughter of an animal itself and its offspring: “

chunks.en: "one day."
chunks.st: One day” (Leviticus 22:28).

chunks.en: Just as the "one day" said in the story
chunks.st: Just as concerning the phrase “one day” that is stated in the act of Creation,

chunks.en: of Creation, the day goes after the night,
chunks.st: the day follows the night,

chunks.en: so too the "one day" said
chunks.st: so too concerning the phrase “one day” that is stated

chunks.en: about "it and its child,"
chunks.st: with regard to the slaughter of an animal itself and its offspring,

chunks.en: the day goes after the night.
chunks.st: the day follows the night.
